meta.title: Jumperless V5 — LED blink (node-numbered)
meta.intro: A single LED driven from the top rail through a current-limiting resistor to ground, laid out on a Jumperless V5. Because you make connections in software on a Jumperless, every terminal strip is labeled with its ROUTING NODE NUMBER (1–30 on the top half, 31–60 on the bottom) — the same numbers you'll type when you route the nets.
notes: The Jumperless is physically a 30-column half-breadboard. The strip directly across the center ravine from node N is node N+30.

notes.html: Rails: TOP_RAIL and BOTTOM_RAIL are the two adjustable rails; the companion line is GND (the bottom rail is often used as GND). The +/− line assignment within each rail pair follows standard breadboard silkscreen — confirm against your board's red/blue markings.

notes: In software you'd route: node 10 → TOP_RAIL, node 12 → GND. The physical jumpers below mirror those two routes plus the LED and resistor.
buildOrder: Seat the LED across nodes 10 (anode, long leg) and 11 (cathode).
Place the 330Ω resistor from node 11 to node 12.
Jumper node 10 to TOP_RAIL, and node 12 to GND (or route those two nets in software).
Set TOP_RAIL to ~3.3 V and the LED lights.
checks: LED long leg (anode) is on node 10, short leg (cathode) on node 11.
TOP_RAIL reaches node 10; node 12 reaches GND.
